question: Why is a thin metal foil used in Rutherford’s $\alpha$-particle scattering experiment? Give reason.

options.A: A thick foil is used so each alpha particle scatters from many nuclei and gives a larger measurable deflection.
options.B: A thin foil ensures that alpha particles lose all of their kinetic energy before scattering.
options.C: A thin foil is used so most alpha particles interact with only one or very few nuclei. This avoids multiple deflections, allowing the observed scattering angle to be interpreted as due to the electrostatic interaction with a single nucleus.
options.D: Thin foil is used because alpha particles cannot pass through a thick foil at any energy.
